research_question: Do the higher Fourier frequencies in standard g8, rather than the number of trainable Fourier components alone, drive its larger reference-to-Q.ANT logit error and prediction disagreement?
observations: Exp014 found the Q.ANT-specific residual increased strongly with frequency.
Exp017 found g8 had about 1.99x the mean absolute logit error and about 1.81x the prediction disagreements of g4.
A frequency-controlled g8 can retain eight trainable amplitude/phase components and the same parameter count as standard g8 while replacing frequencies 5-8 with a second copy of frequencies 1-4.
hypothesis: Compared with standard g8 k=[1..8], frequency-controlled g8 k=[1,2,3,4,1,2,3,4] will reduce reference-to-Q.ANT logit error and prediction disagreement while retaining reference accuracy closer to standard g8 than to a capacity-reduced g4 baseline.
falsification_criterion: The frequency hypothesis is not supported if frequency-controlled g8 fails to reduce both mean absolute logit error and prediction disagreement versus standard g8, or if any reduction is accompanied by a material loss of reference accuracy that removes the intended capacity control.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
Three seeds and three epochs limit precision.
Repeated low frequencies preserve parameter count but do not guarantee the same representational function class as distinct frequencies 1-8.
